html:
Dadabhai Naoroji was the elder statesman of early Indian nationalism. He showed with figures that British rule was making India poorer, and he was the first Indian elected to the British Parliament.

He was a Parsi (see the Parsis), born poor in 1825 and schooled in Bombay, where he became the first Indian professor at Elphinstone College, teaching mathematics. In 1855 he went to London as partner in an Indian trading firm and stayed, on and off, for fifty years.

His main idea is the "drain of wealth". India paid Britain each year for pensions, the salaries of British officials, interest and the cost of an army used abroad, and got nothing back. He put the drain at £30 to 40 million a year and worked out the average Indian income at 20 rupees a year. He set the case out in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India, published in 1901. The title made his point: Britain was not ruling India by its own stated principles.

He helped found the Indian National Congress and was its president three times. In 1892 he won the London seat of Central Finsbury for the Liberals by five votes. As Congress president in 1906 he named swaraj, self-rule, as its goal. Young Gandhi and Jinnah both learnt from him.
